subject: Energy
title: Airborne Wind Energy
description: A fast breakdown of Airborne Wind Energy for builders.

hook.text: Airborne wind energy uses kites or drones tethered to the ground—harvesting faster, steadier winds at high altitude.

buildup.text: At 500m altitude, winds blow 2–3x stronger than at tower height—containing up to 8x more energy per square meter.

discovery.text: Makani (a Google X project) flew a 600 kW energy kite—proving that a tethered wing could generate meaningful power.

twist.text: Makani was shut down in 2020—the technology worked but couldn't compete with rapidly cheapening wind turbines.

climax.text: Other startups (Kitemill, SkySails) continue developing the concept—targeting remote or offshore applications.

punchline.text: Fly a kite, make power—high winds hold untapped energy.

quiz.question: Why is wind stronger at high altitudes?
options: Less air resistance above ground obstacles
